newsitem.title: POLAND: Honest Pole turns $100,000 find over to police.
newsitem.headline: Honest Pole turns $100,000 find over to police.

text.p: A low-paid railway worker has turned over to police a $100,000 cash ransom he accidentally found near a rail crossing in southern Poland, a senior police official said on Thursday.
The money was the ransom a Polish-Ukrainian gang of kidnappers had demanded after abducting the 40-year-old wife of a prominent Krakow businessman.
Deputy provincial police commander Jozef Semik told a news conference reported by PAP news agency that police on Wednesday had arrested a Ukrainian citizen involved in the kidnapping.

The unnamed railway switchman found the money earlier this week in a ditch near the rail crossing at Plaszow where he works and immediately reported his find to police. For fear of his life, he asked not to be identified.
Semik did not reveal whether the police had engineered or monitored the ransom drop, nor why the kidnappers had released their victim without receiving the money, PAP reported.
It was also unclear whether the railwayman would be rewarded for his honesty.
